messages.subject: Minor Syntax Issue with simulateData()
parts:
I'm not sure how likely it is that this will ever come up for anyone else, but I figured it was worth mentioning.

Earlier, I simulated data using the following model syntax:

model<-"
.7*y1+.7*y2+.7*y3
y1~~.51*y1
y2~~.51*y2
y3~~.51*y3
"

I accidentally forgot the "f1=~" syntax in the first line. However the code still ran, and produced data with the following covariance matrix:

            y1          y2           y3
y1 0.517873362  0.03482017  0.008008696
y2 0.034820169  0.55445170 -0.023833260
y3 0.008008696 -0.02383326  0.510111929

So essentially, it just skipped the problematic line, and simulated data as though it weren't present. The issue is that this does not throw an error or warning. While I wouldn't call this a bug, I think it might be beneficial to throw a warning when a line of syntax (other than blank lines or comments) doesn't contain any =s or ~s and is thus skipped.

Jordan

Indeed. Thanks for reporting this. It is a side-product of the fact that
you can 'split' a formula over multiple lines. But we naively assume the
first line always contains an operator. Will fix this soon.

Yves.
